limitations_and_boundaries: Study uses only one cancer cell line (A549) and CAFs from three patients; results may not generalize.
mRNA expression analysis limited to selected factors; other biochemical factors may be involved.
In vitro model may not fully recapitulate in vivo tumor microenvironment.

research_questions.statement: How do cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) with varying matrix-remodeling capacities influence cancer cell invasion?

additional_provenance.text_excerpt: In Cases 1 and 2 of this study, positive correlations between the number of invaded cancer cells and the extents of the remodeling areas generated by CAF clones were observed. The local invasion of cancer cells in Cases 1 and 2 was thought to depend on the extents of the remodeling areas generated by each CAF clone

provenance.text_excerpt: The number of invaded cancer cells was moderately and strongly correlated with the remodeling areas generated by each CAF clone originating from Cases 1 and 2 (R2 value = 0.53 and 0.68, respectively), suggesting that the remodeling areas in the ECM may determine the number of invaded cancer cells.

claims.statement: In Cases 1 and 2 (early-stage lung adenocarcinoma), cancer cell invasion is dependent on the extent of ECM remodeling areas generated by CAFs.

additional_provenance.text_excerpt: cancer cell invasion was not correlated with the extents of the remodeling areas of CAF clones in Case 3. Although the cancer cells invaded by following the CAFs into the matrix in all three cases, the cancer cell invasion in Case 3 might have depended on not the extents of the remodeling areas, but on biochemical factors

provenance.text_excerpt: In contrast, the number of invaded cancer cells was not correlated with the remodeling areas generated by CAF clones originating from Case 3, suggesting that factors other than the remodeling areas might determine the number of invading cancer cells.

claims.statement: In Case 3 (advanced-stage lung adenocarcinoma), cancer cell invasion is not correlated with the extent of ECM remodeling areas generated by CAFs, suggesting dependence on biochemical factors.

provenance.text_excerpt: we measured the relative mRNA expressions of hepatocyte growth factor (HGF), TGFβ1, CXCL12, fibronectin, and tenascin C in the CAF clones, but no significant positive correlations between the expression level of each mRNA and the number of invaded cancer cells were observed... the negative correlation between the number of invaded cancer cells and the expression level of tenascin C was found

claims.statement: No significant positive correlations were found between mRNA expression levels of HGF, TGFβ1, CXCL12, fibronectin, or tenascin C in CAF clones and the number of invaded cancer cells; a negative correlation was observed for tenascin C.

experiments_or_tasks: Co-culture of A549 lung adenocarcinoma cells with single-cell-derived CAF clones from three patients (Case 1, 2, 3) in a collagen invasion assay; measurement of remodeling areas and invaded cancer cell numbers over 48 hours.

methods.name: Collagen invasion assay
methods.protocol_description: 0.3% type I collagen gel coated on 96-well plates; cells plated at 5×10^4 cells/well (co-culture: 2.5×10^4 CAFs and 2.5×10^4 A549 cells); wound made after 1 h; cells embedded in collagen gel; time-lapse imaging every 3 h for 48 h using IncuCyte; at least eight fields per condition in two or more independent experiments.

methods.name: Image analysis
methods.protocol_description: CL-Quant software used to detect cell region, invasion region, invaded CAF region, remodeling area, and count invaded cancer cells (red fluorescence). Invasion indices calculated as average remodeling area/invasion region and average number of invaded cancer cells/invasion region ×1000.

methods.name: Statistical analysis
methods.protocol_description: Student's t test; coefficient of determination (R2) calculated; P < 0.05 considered significant.
